record.original_question: Is there an almost simple but not simple group which is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph? Note that if a group G is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg– Kegel graph, then G is recognizable by its Gruenberg–Kegel graph, and therefore G is almost simple(P. J. Cameron, N. V. Maslova, J. Algebra, 607(2022), 186–213).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite group $G$, the Gruenberg–Kegel graph (prime graph) $\Gamma(G)$ is the graph whose vertex set is the set of prime divisors of $|G|$ and in which two distinct primes $r$ and $s$ are adjacent if and only if $G$ contains an element of order $rs$.

Say that a finite group $G$ is recognizable by its Gruenberg–Kegel graph if every finite group $H$ with $\Gamma(H) = \Gamma(G)$ (equality of labeled graphs on the set of prime divisors) is isomorphic to $G$, and that $G$ is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph if every finite group $H$ such that $\Gamma(H)$ is isomorphic (as an abstract unlabeled graph) to $\Gamma(G)$ is isomorphic to $G$.

Recall that a finite group $G$ is called almost simple if there exists a non-abelian finite simple group $S$ such that $S \trianglelefteq G \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$; in particular every non-abelian finite simple group is almost simple.

It is known that if $G$ is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph, then $G$ is recognizable by its Gruenberg–Kegel graph, and consequently $G$ is almost simple.

Question: Does there exist a finite almost simple group that is not simple and is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint on characterization of groups by the isomorphism type of the Gruenberg–Kegel graph explicitly poses this exact question as an open problem, noting that no almost-simple-but-not-simple example has been exhibited; only simple examples (such as certain $E_8(q)$ and ${}^2E_6(2)$) are known to be recognizable by the isomorphism type of the Gruenberg–Kegel graph.

status_evidence.title: On characterization of groups by isomorphism type of Gruenberg–Kegel graph
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 2. Is there an almost simple but not simple group which is recognizable by isomorphism type of Gruenberg–Kegel graph?
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem; only simple-group examples are known.

status_evidence.title: Recognisability of the sporadic groups by the isomorphism types of their prime graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies recognizability by isomorphism type of the prime graph for sporadic simple groups.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; existing examples of recognizability by graph isomorphism type concern simple groups.
